meta.subject: physics
meta.title: Einstein Physics
meta.note: X6: ages 5–6 Push, Pull, Sink & Float unit (3 lab lessons). X5: ages 7–8 Forces & Friction unit (4 lab lessons + unit check). Ages 9–10: Ramp Racer.

ages-5-6.label: Ages 5–6
ages-5-6.blurb: Push, pull, sink or float — first experiments in Einstein's lab.

units.title: Push, Pull, Sink & Float
units.description: Push a box, pull it back, shove heavy boxes, and drop toys in the water tank. What will happen? Let's find out!

ph-push-or-pull.title: Push or Pull?
ph-push-or-pull.einsteinIntro: Hello, little scientist! Today we move a toy box with pushes and pulls. A push and a pull are both called a FORCE!

panels.speech: A push moves something AWAY from you. Push a swing and — whoosh — away it goes!
A pull brings something TOWARD you, like pulling a wagon by its handle.
A gentle push makes a little slide. A BIG push makes a big slide! Let's try it.

sim.explore: Pick Push or Pull, choose how hard, then press Run it. Where does the box go?

simChecks.prompt: Einstein gives the box a PUSH. Which way will it slide?
simChecks.hint: A push sends things away from you.

simChecks.prompt: Make the box come TOWARD Einstein. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Pushing sends it away. Try a pull!

simChecks.prompt: First a gentle push (8). Then a BIG push (20). Will the big push send the box farther?
simChecks.hint: A bigger push gives a bigger slide.

simChecks.prompt: Push the box past the red flag (2 m)! Run it, then press Check.

goal.label: the box slides past the red flag (2 m)

simChecks.hint: Push harder! Slide How hard? way up.

ph-big-small-push.title: Big Push, Small Push
ph-big-small-push.einsteinIntro: Some boxes are light like a pillow. Some are heavy like a pile of books. Which one is harder to push? Let's test!

panels.speech: The floor grips the box a little. A teeny push can't beat the grip, so the box stays put.
A heavy box needs a BIGGER push to move. A light box zooms with just a small push.
Push hard for far, gentle for near. You're the boss of the box!

sim.explore: Try a light box and a heavy box. How hard do you need to push each one?

simChecks.prompt: Einstein gives a box a teeny-tiny push (just 3). Will the box move?
simChecks.hint: A tiny push can't beat the floor's grip.

simChecks.prompt: Einstein pushes a LIGHT box (1 kg). Then he pushes a HEAVY box (4 kg) just as hard. Will the heavy box go farther?
simChecks.hint: Heavy things are harder to get moving.

simChecks.prompt: This box is HEAVY (4 kg). Push it past the blue flag (1 m)! Run it, then press Check.

goal.label: the heavy box slides past the blue flag (1 m)

simChecks.hint: A heavy box needs a really BIG push. Try more than 22.

simChecks.prompt: Now a LIGHT box (1 kg). Give it a gentle push so it stops in the green zone, between the blue and red flags. Run it, then press Check.

goal.label: the box stops in the green zone (1 m to 2 m)

simChecks.hint: Too far? Push more gently. Try about 6 or 7.

ph-sink-or-float.title: Sink or Float?
ph-sink-or-float.einsteinIntro: Splash time! We drop things into my water tank. Will they float on top or sink to the bottom? Guess first, then test!

panels.speech: Water pushes UP on everything you put in it. That push helps things float.
Wood, apples and rubber ducks float. Rocks, coins and keys sink to the bottom.
Here's a surprise: big doesn't mean sink! A huge log floats, but a tiny coin sinks.

sim.explore: Pick something, press Run it, and watch: does it float or sink? Try them all!

simChecks.prompt: Plop! Einstein drops a ROCK into the water. Will it float or sink?
simChecks.hint: Rocks are heavy for their size.

simChecks.prompt: Now an APPLE. Will it float or sink?
simChecks.hint: Apples have lots of air inside them.

simChecks.prompt: Pick something that FLOATS, drop it in, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Try the wooden block or the rubber duck.

simChecks.prompt: This log is BIG and heavy. Will it float or sink?
simChecks.hint: Big doesn't mean sink. Logs are made of wood!

simChecks.prompt: The duck floats. Now find something SMALL that SINKS! Drop it in, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Try the coin or the key.

ages-7-8.label: Ages 7–8
ages-7-8.blurb: Forces & friction: slopes, surfaces and mass in Einstein's ramp lab.

units.title: Forces & Friction
units.description: Why do things slide or stick? Test slopes, surfaces and heavy blocks in Einstein's ramp lab, then take the unit check!

ph-ramp-slide-or-stick.title: Slide or Stick? The Ramp Lab
ph-ramp-slide-or-stick.einsteinIntro: Welcome to my ramp lab! Gravity pulls the block down the slope, and friction — the ramp's grip — tries to hold it. Who wins? Let's experiment!

panels.speech: Gravity always pulls things down. On a ramp, part of that pull drags the block along the slope.
Friction is grip between the block and the ramp. Grippy surfaces hold on; slippery ones let go.
Make the ramp steeper and gravity's slope pull gets stronger. When it beats the grip — WHOOSH, the block slides!

sim.explore: Move the sliders and press Run it. Can you find the angle where the block starts to slide?

simChecks.prompt: The ramp is tilted just 10° and the grip is 0.5. Will the block slide?
simChecks.hint: A gentle slope only pulls a little — and a grip of 0.5 holds on tight.

simChecks.prompt: Tilt the ramp until the block slides! (The grip is locked at 0.5.) Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Steeper ramps pull harder. Try more than 27°.

simChecks.prompt: At 35°, a 1 kg block races to the bottom. Will a 5 kg block get there faster, slower, or at the same time?
simChecks.hint: A heavier block gets a bigger pull AND a bigger grip — they grow together!

simChecks.prompt: Make the block reach the bottom in less than 1.2 seconds. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Make the ramp steeper, or the surface less grippy.

ph-ramp-steeper-faster.title: Steeper Means Faster?
ph-ramp-steeper-faster.einsteinIntro: Big question, little scientist: does a steeper ramp make the block go faster? Let's race and find out!

panels.speech: A steeper ramp tips more of gravity's pull along the slope. More pull means the block speeds up faster.
But if the ramp is too gentle, the grip wins and the block won't move at all!
Scientists test one thing at a time. Today we only change the angle and watch the clock.

sim.explore: Change the ramp angle and press Run it. Watch the timer: which angle wins the race?

simChecks.prompt: A block slides down a 30° ramp. If we tilt the ramp to 45°, will it reach the bottom faster, slower, or at the same time?
simChecks.hint: Steeper ramps pull harder along the slope.

simChecks.prompt: Make the block reach the bottom in less than 1 second. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Go steep! Try more than 45°.

simChecks.prompt: The ramp is tilted 20° and the grip is 0.4. Will the block slide?
simChecks.hint: A gentle slope only pulls a little. Is it enough to beat a grip of 0.4?

simChecks.prompt: Make a slow, gentle slide: the block should take between 1 and 1.5 seconds. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Find the angle where it JUST starts sliding, then nudge it a little steeper.

ph-ramp-surfaces.title: Ice, Wood or Carpet?
ph-ramp-surfaces.einsteinIntro: Ice is slippery, carpet is grippy. Let's see how the surface changes what our block does!

panels.speech: Friction is the grip between two surfaces. Bumpy, rough surfaces grab on tight.
Smooth surfaces like ice barely grip at all, so things slide even on a gentle slope.
That's why we sprinkle sand on icy roads: more grip, less sliding!

sim.explore: Change the grip slider from icy (low) to grippy (high) and press Run it. When does the block stick?

simChecks.prompt: The ramp is covered in ice (grip 0.1) and tilted only 10°. Will the block slide?
simChecks.hint: Ice hardly grips at all, so even a tiny slope can win.

simChecks.prompt: The ramp is covered in thick carpet (grip 0.9) and tilted 30°. Will the block slide?
simChecks.hint: Carpet grabs on tight. A 30° slope isn't steep enough to beat it.

simChecks.prompt: The ramp is locked at 35°. Change the surface so the block STAYS PUT. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Make the surface grippier. Try a grip of 0.75 or more.

simChecks.prompt: A block slides down a wooden ramp at 40°. Now we cover the ramp in ice. Will it reach the bottom faster, slower, or at the same time?
simChecks.hint: Less grip means less friction holding the block back.

ph-ramp-heavy-light.title: Heavy vs Light: The Big Race
ph-ramp-heavy-light.einsteinIntro: Will a heavy block beat a light block down the ramp? Most people guess yes. Let's test it like real scientists!

panels.speech: A heavier block gets a BIGGER pull from gravity. Sounds like it should win, right?
But a heavier block also presses harder on the ramp, so friction grips it harder too.
The extra pull and the extra grip grow together. Let's see who wins!

sim.explore: Change the block mass, press Run it, and compare the times. Does heavy beat light?

simChecks.prompt: On a 35° ramp, a 1 kg block races an 8 kg block. Will the heavy block get there faster, slower, or at the same time?
simChecks.hint: More mass means more pull AND more grip, and they grow together.

simChecks.prompt: A heavy 10 kg block sits on a 20° ramp with a grip of 0.5. Will it slide?
simChecks.hint: Heavy or light, the slope has to beat the grip. Mass doesn't change who wins.

simChecks.prompt: The block is locked at 8 kg. Make it reach the bottom in less than 1 second. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: You can't change the mass, so what else makes it faster? Try a steeper ramp.

simChecks.prompt: At 40°, a 2 kg block hits the bottom at some speed. Will a 0.5 kg block be faster, slower, or the same speed at the bottom?
simChecks.hint: Remember the race: mass cancels out!

ph-ff-unit-check.title: Forces & Friction Check ⭐
ph-ff-unit-check.einsteinIntro: Time to show what you know! Use everything you learned about slopes, grip and mass.

panels.speech: Remember: the slope's pull has to beat the grip before anything slides.
Steeper ramps and slippery surfaces make blocks go faster. Mass? It doesn't change the race!
Predict first, then test it in the lab. That's how scientists work. You've got this!

sim.explore: Warm up in the lab: try every slider once, then start the check.

simChecks.prompt: The ramp is tilted 40° and the grip is 0.5. Will the block slide?
simChecks.hint: 40° is pretty steep. Can a grip of 0.5 hold on?

simChecks.prompt: A block slides down a 30° ramp. We tilt it to 50°. Will it reach the bottom faster, slower, or at the same time?
simChecks.hint: Steeper ramps pull harder.

simChecks.prompt: On a 40° ramp, will a 6 kg block beat a 2 kg block to the bottom?

choices.label: Yes, the 6 kg block is faster
No, the 6 kg block is slower

simChecks.hint: Think back to the Big Race.

simChecks.prompt: The ramp is locked at 40°. Make the block stay put. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Turn the grip way up, past 0.85.

simChecks.prompt: Now make the block reach the bottom in less than 1 second. Run it, then press Check.
simChecks.hint: Steep ramp, low grip. Go!

ages-9-10.label: Ages 9–10
ages-9-10.blurb: Ramps, friction & acceleration — measure it in Einstein's lab.

units.title: Ramps & Acceleration
units.description: Measure how fast a block speeds up — and see friction and gravity at work.

ph-ramp-acceleration.title: Ramp Racer: Friction & Acceleration
ph-ramp-acceleration.einsteinIntro: Scientists measure! Today we race blocks down a ramp and discover the rule for how fast they speed up.

panels.speech: To START sliding, the slope pull must beat static friction: tan θ > μs. Until then — stuck!
Once sliding, kinetic friction (μk) is smaller. The block speeds up with a = g(sin θ − μk·cos θ).
Notice what's missing? Mass! It cancels out. Change g instead — try the Moon!

sim.explore: Run a few races. Watch the acceleration readout as you change θ, μk and g.

simChecks.prompt: θ = 30°, μs = 0.7, μk = 0.5. Does the block start to slide?
simChecks.hint: Compare tan 30° ≈ 0.58 with μs.

simChecks.prompt: Set the ramp so the acceleration is about 3 m/s² (±0.3). Gravity is locked to Earth.
simChecks.hint: a = g(sin θ − μk·cos θ). With μk = 0.25, try an angle in the 30s.

simChecks.prompt: θ = 40°, μs = 0.3, μk = 0.2, g = 9.8. What is the acceleration? Use a = g(sin θ − μk·cos θ).
On the Moon (g = 1.6 m/s²), get the block to the bottom of the 2 m ramp in under 3 seconds.
simChecks.hint: Weak gravity means a slow start — go steeper and slipperier.
